text.p: Pogo Producing Co said said results from three wildcat wells drilled on the new seismic structure in the Gulf of Thailand known as "Benchamas North" were disappointing.

The wells encountered a number of prospective oil and gas sands, but only modest accumulations of hydrocarbons were found in each well, the company said. No drill stem testing was conducted in the three wells.
The wells were drilled five to 10 miles north of the separate and prolific "Benchamas" structure area, where nine productive Benchamas wells already have been drilled to date.
Pogo owns 46.34 percent and serves as operator of Block B8/32. A silimar interst is held Rutherford-Moran Oil Corp, while a Thai corporation, Sophonpanich Co Ltd owns 7.4 percent.
"The results of these three Benchamas North wells, while disappointing, do not condemn Benchamas North, which will continue to be evaluated in anticipation of future drilling," Pogo said.

It said the Benchamas Field is being developed on an accelerated basis with first production target for about April 1999. Other distinctly separate seismic structures lying within Block B8/32 still offer the partners other exploratory opportunities, such as the Maliwan structure and the Pattalung-Yungthong trend, both of which are expected to be explored before year-end 1997.

The Tantawan Field, on stream since February 1, is doing extremely well, Pogo said, and resumption of drilling at the Benchamas prospect will allow the concession holders to drill future platform-locating wells.
Some 50 wells have now been drilled on Block B8/32 by Pogo and its partners, and there are 30 wells in the present budget planned for 1997 drilling.
